## Teaching

Over the last years I have been teaching a variety of courses in the following areas:

-   Political Behavior and Public Opinion
-   Political Participation
-   Political Methodology
-   Political Geography
-   Introduction to R
-   Mapping at the University of Barcelona (*Analista de dades per a l'anàlisi política i la gestió pública*). Among other things, we learn how to make interactive maps (see an example <a href="mapa_repressio.html" target="_blank">here</a>)

## PhD supervision

I am always delighted to supervise PhD students. Guiding them through their doctoral journey—helping refine questions, develop rigorous methodologies, and communicate findings—is both inspiring and a learning experience for me. I value curiosity, independence, and creativity, and I strive to provide a supportive environment where students can grow as scholars and contribute meaningfully to political science.

Meet them 👇

-   Joaquín Rozas-Bugueño <a href="https://sites.google.com/view/joaquin-rozas-bugueno" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> <img src="../../images/webpage.jpg" alt="Rozas-Bugueño Website" style="height:20px; vertical-align:middle;"/></a> His doctoral dissertation focused on how social movements influence public opinion and political behavior, especially following major events like the 2019 protests in Chile.

-   Irene Rodríguez <a href="https://irenerodriguezlopez.github.io/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> <img src="../../images/webpage.jpg" alt="Irene Website" style="height:20px; vertical-align:middle;"/></a> Her doctoral thesis focuses on contemporary challenges to democracy, including studies of policy effects following the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as radical right parties and the surge of social network use by political parties. She is part of the [COVIDEU project](../projects/covideu/index.qmd).

-   Emanuele Murgolo <a href="https://www.upf.edu/web/demosoc/members/-/asset_publisher/JRxS2cKgUsHo/content/murgolo-emanuele/maximized" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> <img src="../../images/webpage.jpg" alt="Emanuele Website" style="height:20px; vertical-align:middle;"/></a> His doctoral dissertation analyzes whether the geography of political inequalities between Black and White communities in the US determines the socioeconomic gap between them.

-   Elena Romanin <a href="https://elenaromanin.github.io/index.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> <img src="../../images/webpage.jpg" alt="Elena Website" style="height:20px; vertical-align:middle;"/></a> She explores the determinants of people's support for, or rejection of, climate change policies and related behaviors, primarily using survey data and experiments. She is member of the [Attclimate project](../projects/attclimate/index.qmd).

-   Sofija Riegger. Her thesis examines how exposure to violence shapes electoral behavior in post-conflict settings. It investigates whether communities reject parties associated with perpetrators and how the intensity and timing of conflict influence voting patterns. She is part of the [VEARLYDEM project](../projects/vearlydem/index.qmd).

Completed PhD 🎓

-   Nikandros Ioannidis. He defended in November 2024 his dissertation *Worlds apart: The impact of (in)congruence on electoral behaviour: When voters and parties do not align* \[[Access](https://repositori.upf.edu/items/6c436f2b-0262-4138-957e-b169ec5df7ce)\].
